STEP-PLAN/v3
ELECTION: NONE
ASSUMED STRUCTURE: Asset/Stock hybrid acquisition — election to be confirmed at STEP-03
ASSUMED CLOSE DATE: 2026-10-15
PREPARED: 2026-10-03

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PHASE A — PRE-CLOSING (T-10 TO T-1 BUSINESS DAYS)
─────────────────────────────────────────────

STEP-01: BRING-DOWN DILIGENCE — REPRESENTATIONS & WARRANTIES
  Owner: Buyer's counsel + Tax counsel
  Deadline: T-5 (2026-10-08)
  Action Items:
    a. Re-confirm all Seller tax reps as of Closing Date (no material change since signing).
    b. Verify no new tax liens, IRS notices, or open audits surfaced post-signing.
    c. Pull Secretary of State good-standing certificates for Target and all subsidiaries (dated ≤ 10 days before close).
    d. Confirm no changes to Target's EIN, fiscal year, or S-corporation/partnership status that would affect election eligibility.
    e. Re-confirm absence of any "disqualifying event" under IRC §338(h)(10) or §336(e) (e.g., step-acquisition timing, QSP window).
  Tax Impact Note: Stale or inaccurate bring-down could invalidate R&W insurance coverage; S-corp status change post-signing nullifies §338(h)(10) eligibility.
  Dependency: STEP-02, STEP-03

STEP-02: ELECTION DECISION — FINAL CONFIRMATION
  Owner: Tax counsel (Buyer & Seller) + CFO
  Deadline: T-5 (2026-10-08)
  Action Items:
    a. Run final purchase-price allocation model under both asset-deal and stock-deal (with §338(h)(10) or §336(e)) scenarios using executed LOI price + working capital peg.
    b. Confirm Seller's tax basis in Target stock and built-in gain/loss positions.
    c. Confirm Buyer's stepped-up basis benefit vs. Seller's incremental tax cost; document agreed gross-up (if any) in writing.
    d. If §338(h)(10) elected: confirm (i) Target is a domestic corporation, (ii) Seller is a corporate shareholder, (iii) Buyer acquires ≥ 80% in a single qualified stock purchase (QSP).
    e. If §336(e) elected: confirm Target is a domestic corporation and Seller is a corporation (S-corp or C-corp); note §336(e) does NOT require corporate Buyer.
    f. Document final election decision in Tax Structuring Memo (attach to closing binder).
  Tax Impact Note: §338(h)(10) treated-asset-sale gain flows through consolidated/S-corp return; double tax avoided for S-corp Sellers. §336(e) available when §338(h)(10) is not (e.g., non-corporate Buyer).
  Dependency: STEP-01, STEP-05

STEP-03: PURCHASE PRICE ALLOCATION — PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE
  Owner: Tax counsel + Financial advisor
  Deadline: T-3 (2026-10-10)
  Action Items:
    a. Prepare preliminary §1060 allocation (Class I–VII) consistent with final agreed enterprise value.
    b. Identify any contingent consideration (earnout) and document treatment under Reg. §1.338-6/-7.
    c. Circulate draft Form 8594 (or Form 8883 if §338(h)(10)) to both parties for review and sign-off.
    d. Flag any intangible assets (goodwill, customer lists, non-competes) for §197 amortization schedule.
    e. Confirm working capital true-up methodology and its effect on Class II/III allocation.
  Tax Impact Note: Agreed allocation is binding on both parties; inconsistent treatment triggers §6721 penalties. Non-competes allocated to Class VI are §197 amortizable over 15 years.
  Dependency: STEP-02

STEP-04: CONSENT & APPROVAL CHECKLIST
  Owner: Deal counsel + Corporate secretary
  Deadline: T-3 (2026-10-10)
  Action Items:
    a. Board resolutions — Seller entity: authorize sale, election filing, and funds disbursement.
    b. Board resolutions — Buyer entity: authorize acquisition, financing drawdown, and election.
    c. Shareholder/member consents — confirm requisite approval percentage obtained (check charter/operating agreement).
    d. Third-party consents:
         i.   Material contracts with change-of-control provisions (identify top 10 by revenue impact).
         ii.  Real property leases (landlord consents).
         iii. Government/regulatory licenses and permits (transfer or reissuance filings).
         iv.  Lender consents / payoff letters for existing debt (confirm payoff amount good through Closing Date + 5 days).
    e. HSR / antitrust clearance — confirm waiting period expired or early termination granted; retain FTC/DOJ confirmation letter.
    f. CFIUS — confirm no filing obligation or clearance obtained.
    g. State-level bulk sales/transfer notifications (UCC lien search in all jurisdictions where Target has assets).
  Tax Impact Note: Missing lender payoff letters create lien-survival risk; UCC lapse triggers successor liability under bulk-sale statutes in ~22 states.
  Dependency: STEP-06

STEP-05: FUNDS FLOW MEMORANDUM — FINAL VERSION
  Owner: Buyer's counsel + Escrow agent
  Deadline: T-2 (2026-10-13)
  Action Items:
    a. Identify all payment sources (equity, debt, rollover equity) with wire amounts and account numbers (confirmed by T-2).
    b. Map all payment destinations:
         i.   Seller proceeds (gross purchase price).
         ii.  Payoff of Target indebtedness (wire directly to each lender — confirm good-through date).
         iii. Transaction expenses (legal, banker, accounting — confirm each payee W-9 on file).
         iv.  Escrow deposits (indemnification, R&W insurance, working capital, tax).
         v.   Employee transaction bonuses / stay payments (confirm payroll tax withholding mechanism).
    c. Confirm currency, wire routing/SWIFT codes, and cut-off times (Fed Fedwire closes 18:00 ET; CHIPS closes 17:00 ET).
    d. Confirm net cash to Seller after: (i) indebtedness payoff, (ii) transaction expenses, (iii) escrow holdbacks, (iv) tax withholding (FIRPTA cert or withholding agent arrangement).
    e. FIRPTA: obtain Seller FIRPTA certificate (Form 8288-B or Seller certification under §1445) or arrange withholding.
    f. Final funds flow memo signed by Seller, Buyer, and Escrow Agent.
  Tax Impact Note: Employee transaction bonuses paid by Target are deductible by Target (not Buyer) only if accrued in Target's final short-period return; confirm timing. FIRPTA withholding failure = Buyer liability.
  Dependency: STEP-04, STEP-08

STEP-06: TAX CERTIFICATES & CLEARANCES
  Owner: Tax counsel
  Deadline: T-2 (2026-10-13)
  Action Items:
    a. Obtain state tax clearance certificates in each jurisdiction where Target files (confirm states; typical lead time 2–6 weeks — flag if not yet received).
    b. Obtain sales/use tax clearance or reserve in applicable states.
    c. Obtain payroll tax clearance (state unemployment + workers' comp where applicable).
    d. Confirm no outstanding franchise tax, gross receipts tax, or CAT obligations.
    e. Confirm transfer taxes (real property, stock transfer, documentary stamp) — compute amounts, identify payor, include in funds flow.
  Tax Impact Note: Missing state clearance certificates create successor liability risk for Buyer. Transfer tax computations must be finalized before funding.
  Dependency: STEP-05

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PHASE B — CLOSING DAY (T = 2026-10-15)
─────────────────────────────────────────────

STEP-07: CLOSING DOCUMENT EXECUTION SEQUENCE
  Owner: Deal counsel (coordinate all signatories)
  Deadline: Closing Day — 09:00–12:00 ET (execution window)
  Execution Order & Document Checklist:
    1.  Stock Purchase Agreement / Asset Purchase Agreement — final execution
    2.  Officer's Certificate (Seller) — bring-down of reps and warranties as of Closing Date
    3.  Officer's Certificate (Buyer) — bring-down of reps and warranties as of Closing Date
    4.  Secretary's Certificate (Seller) — board resolutions, charter, good-standing
    5.  Secretary's Certificate (Buyer) — board resolutions, charter, good-standing
    6.  Non-Competition / Non-Solicitation Agreement(s) — key principals
    7.  Employment/Consulting Agreement(s) — rolling key employees
    8.  Transition Services Agreement (TSA) — if applicable
    9.  IP Assignment Agreement — if applicable (asset deal or carved-out IP)
    10. Escrow Agreement — executed by Buyer, Seller, Escrow Agent
    11. FIRPTA Certificate / §1445 Certification
    12. Form 8023 (§338(h)(10) election) or Form 8883 — signed by both parties (if elected)
    13. Payoff letters — executed counterparts confirming payoff amounts
    14. UCC-3 termination statements — executed by lenders (held in escrow pending wire confirmation)
    15. Stock certificates / stock powers (stock deal) — endorsed in blank
    16. Bill of Sale, Assignment & Assumption Agreement (asset deal)
    17. Deed(s) for real property (if applicable) — notarized, held for recording post-funding
    18. Funds Flow Memorandum — countersigned
  Tax Impact Note: Form 8023 must be filed by 15th day of 9th month following the acquisition year; however, both parties must sign on or before Closing. Late filing may be accepted with IRS private letter ruling but creates risk.
  Dependency: All prior steps complete

STEP-08: WIRE SEQUENCE & CONFIRMATION
  Owner: Buyer CFO + Escrow Agent
  Deadline: Closing Day — 12:00–15:00 ET (funding window)
  Action Items:
    a. Buyer initiates equity wire to Escrow Agent (confirm receipt by Escrow Agent).
    b. Buyer initiates debt drawdown — confirm lender wire to Escrow Agent or directly to payees per funds flow.
    c. Escrow Agent releases wires per funds flow memo in the following priority sequence:
         Priority 1: Lender payoffs (to eliminate UCC liens).
         Priority 2: Transaction expenses (legal, banker, advisor).
         Priority 3: Employee bonuses (via Target payroll — confirm withholding).
         Priority 4: Tax escrow deposit.
         Priority 5: Indemnification escrow deposit.
         Priority 6: Working capital escrow deposit.
         Priority 7: Net proceeds to Seller.
    d. Obtain written wire confirmation receipts for all outgoing wires.
    e. Confirm lender receipt of payoff → authorize release of UCC-3 terminations from escrow.
    f. Confirm Seller receipt of net proceeds → deal declared "closed" by mutual written notice.
  Tax Impact Note: If any Priority 1 wire fails, close does not occur (lien not released). Confirm payoff letter "good-through" date covers 2026-10-15 + 3 business days buffer.
  Dependency: STEP-05, STEP-07

STEP-09: CLOSING CONFIRMATION & BINDER ASSEMBLY
  Owner: Deal counsel
  Deadline: Closing Day — 16:00 ET
  Action Items:
    a. Circulate closing confirmation notice to all parties.
    b. Assemble fully executed closing binder (electronic and physical) including all documents from STEP-07.
    c. File deeds and real property transfer instruments with applicable county recorders (same day or next business day).
    d. File UCC-3 termination statements (same day or next business day).
    e. Update corporate books and records of Target — transfer ledger, minute book.
    f. Notify Target employees, customers, and vendors per agreed communication plan.
  Tax Impact Note: Real property deed recording triggers transfer tax payment deadline in most states (typically same day or within 5–30 days).
  Dependency: STEP-08

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PHASE C — POST-CLOSING (T+1 TO T+90)
─────────────────────────────────────────────

STEP-10: TAX FILINGS — ELECTION FORMS & SHORT-PERIOD RETURNS
  Owner: Tax counsel + CPA (Target and Buyer)
  Deadline: See individual items below
  Action Items:
    a. Form 8023 (§338(h)(10)) — file with IRS by 9th month, 15th day after acquisition year end (2027-09-15 if fiscal year = calendar year); confirm both parties' signatures obtained at closing (STEP-07 item 12).
    b. Form 8883 (§338(h)(10) allocation) — attach to each party's timely filed return for acquisition year.
    c. Target short-period return (final S-corp/consolidated return through Closing Date) — prepared by Seller's CPA; due on normal extended deadline.
    d. Buyer stub-period return — confirm Target joins Buyer's consolidated group on day after closing (or same day per §1502 regulations).
    e. FIRPTA withholding — if withholding required, file Form 8288 and 8288-A within 20 days of closing (2026-11-04).
    f. State conformity elections — confirm states that follow federal §338 election vs. states requiring separate asset-sale treatment; file state-level elections where required.
    g. Transfer tax returns — file in applicable states per STEP-06 timeline.
  Tax Impact Note: Failure to file Form 8288 within 20 days results in interest and penalties. States such as CA, NY, IL, PA, and TX have independent filing requirements that do not automatically follow federal election.
  Dependency: STEP-07, STEP-03

STEP-11: PURCHASE PRICE ALLOCATION — FINAL FORM 8594 / 8883
  Owner: Tax counsel + Financial advisor
  Deadline: T+75 (2026-12-29)
  Action Items:
    a. Finalize working capital true-up (typically 60–90 days post-close) and incorporate final adjustment into allocation.
    b. Earnout: document treatment — installment sale or open-transaction as applicable.
    c. Circulate final Form 8594 (or Form 8883) to both parties for signature and concurrent filing.
    d. Attach final allocation schedule to closing binder and tax escrow agreement.
  Tax Impact Note: Both parties must file consistent allocations. Inconsistency triggers §6662 accuracy-related penalty and potential audit flag. Final allocation governs Buyer's depreciable/amortizable basis.
  Dependency: STEP-03, STEP-10

─────────────────────────────────────────────
DEPENDENCY MAP
─────────────────────────────────────────────

  STEP-01 → STEP-02, STEP-03
  STEP-02 → STEP-03, STEP-05
  STEP-03 → STEP-10, STEP-11
  STEP-04 → STEP-06, STEP-07
  STEP-05 → STEP-07, STEP-08
  STEP-06 → STEP-05
  STEP-07 → STEP-08, STEP-09
  STEP-08 → STEP-09, STEP-10
  STEP-09 → STEP-10
  STEP-10 → STEP-11

─────────────────────────────────────────────

TAX-COV-LEDGER/v1
DEAL: [Target Acquisition] — Close Date 2026-10-15
PREPARED: 2026-10-03
ESCROW-RELEASE: 2027-10-15

─────────────────────────────────────────────
POST-CLOSING TAX COVENANTS & DAY-1 TAX DELIVERABLES
─────────────────────────────────────────────

TC-001 | Pre-Closing Tax Returns (Seller Obligation)
  Description: Seller shall prepare and timely file (or cause to be filed) all income tax returns of Target for taxable periods ending on or before the Closing Date, including any short-period S-corporation or consolidated returns triggered by the transaction.
  Responsible Party: Seller (with Buyer review right ≥ 30 days before filing)
  Deadline: Per applicable statutory deadlines (federal: 2027-09-15 extended; state: varies)
  Tax Impact: Seller bears tax liability for pre-closing periods; Buyer indemnified for any deficiency attributable to pre-closing periods up to indemnification escrow cap.
  Escrow Trigger: Pre-closing tax liability assessed post-close draws from TC-escrow (see TC-007).

TC-002 | Straddle Period Allocation
  Description: For any taxable period beginning before and ending after the Closing Date ("Straddle Period"), income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit shall be allocated between pre- and post-closing periods using the closing-of-books method for items that can be specifically allocated and the daily-proration method for all other items, consistent with Reg. §1.1502-76(b).
  Responsible Party: Buyer prepares; Seller reviews and approves within 30 days of receipt.
  Deadline: Straddle period return due per normal deadline (estimated T+12 months).
  Tax Impact: Seller responsible for pre-closing Straddle Period tax; Buyer responsible for post-closing portion. Dispute mechanism: binding arbitration by Big-4 accounting firm selected by mutual agreement within 30 days.

TC-003 | §338(h)(10) / §336(e) Election Filing
  Description: If either election was executed at Closing (per STEP-07, item 12), Buyer and Seller shall jointly and timely file Form 8023 (§338(h)(10)) or the applicable §336(e) statement with IRS by the required deadline. Neither party shall revoke or amend the election without written consent of the other party.
  Responsible Party: Tax counsel (joint obligation)
  Deadline: 9th month, 15th day following acquisition year (2027-09-15 for calendar-year Target)
  Tax Impact: Election is irrevocable once filed; revocation requires IRS consent (rare). Failure to file timely may require PLR to cure; cost borne equally unless attributable to one party's failure.
  NOTE: ELECTION: NONE assumed unless confirmed otherwise at STEP-02.

TC-004 | Purchase Price Allocation Consistency
  Description: Buyer and Seller each covenant to report the acquisition consistently with the agreed §1060 / §338 allocation (Form 8594 or Form 8883), to file such forms with their respective returns, and to notify the other party promptly upon receipt of any IRS inquiry or proposed reallocation.
  Responsible Party: Each party for its own filings; Tax counsel coordinates.
  Deadline: File with each party's return for the acquisition year; final allocation per STEP-11 (T+75).
  Tax Impact: Inconsistent filing = §6662 penalty exposure + audit risk for both parties. Escrow may be drawn to fund any agreed allocation adjustment reimbursement.

TC-005 | Transfer Taxes
  Description: All transfer, documentary, stamp, recording, and similar taxes arising from the transaction shall be paid by [____ — confirm allocation in APA; typically 50/50 or Buyer bears]. Payor shall prepare and file all applicable returns; other party shall cooperate and execute any required instruments.
  Responsible Party: Per APA Section [___]
  Deadline: Per applicable state deadlines (most within 30 days of Closing Date; NY: 15 days; CA: same day recording; FL: same day recording)
  Tax Impact: Late payment triggers interest at state statutory rates (range: 5%–12% annualized) plus penalties up to 25% of tax owed in certain states.

TC-006 | Tax Refunds — Pre-Closing Periods
  Description: Any tax refund (including interest thereon) attributable to a pre-closing taxable period of Target shall be for the account of Seller. Buyer shall promptly remit any such refund received by Target post-closing to Seller, net of any reasonable out-of-pocket costs incurred by Buyer in obtaining such refund.
  Responsible Party: Buyer (remittance obligation); Seller (entitlement)
  Deadline: Remittance within 10 business days of receipt by Buyer or Target.
  Tax Impact: Includes refunds arising from amended returns, carry-back claims, or audit settlements for pre-closing periods.

TC-007 | Tax Escrow — Holdback & Release Schedule
  Description: At Closing, [___ amount — confirm in funds flow per STEP-05] shall be deposited into a separate tax escrow account to secure (i) Seller's indemnification obligations for pre-closing taxes, (ii) any §338 election-related tax gross-up, and (iii) any open-year audit settlements.
  Responsible Party: Escrow Agent administers; Buyer controls release instructions subject to APA terms.
  ESCROW-RELEASE: 2027-10-15 (subject to extension if any tax audit is pending or unresolved as of that date; extension period = duration of pending audit + 90 days)
  Partial Release Triggers:
    — Statute of limitations expiry for each pre-closing tax year (generally 3 years from filing; 6 years if substantial omission).
    — Audit closure with no material deficiency.
    — Written agreement of Buyer and Seller.
  Tax Impact: Escrowed amounts are not income to Seller until released; confirm escrow agreement provides for interest to be credited to Seller.

TC-008 | Tax Indemnification — Seller Obligations
  Description: Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer Indemnitees from and against any Losses attributable to: (i) Taxes of Target for any pre-closing taxable period; (ii) Taxes of any consolidated, affiliated, or combined group of which Target was a member for any pre-closing period; (iii) Taxes resulting from breach of Seller's tax representations; (iv) any §338 recapture, if applicable.
  Responsible Party: Seller
  Cap: [___% of purchase price — confirm in APA indemnification article]
  Survival: Tax reps survive until 60 days after expiration of applicable statute of limitations (including extensions and waivers).
  Deadline: Claims must be asserted within survival period.
  Tax Impact: Seller indemnity is Buyer's primary recourse for pre-closing tax exposures; R&W insurance is secondary (subject to retention/deductible).

TC-009 | Tax Indemnification — Buyer Obligations
  Description: Buyer shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Seller Indemnitees from and against any Losses attributable to: (i) Taxes of Target for any post-closing taxable period; (ii) any breach by Buyer of its obligations under TC-003 or TC-004; (iii) any §338 election tax cost borne by Seller to the extent a gross-up was agreed and not paid at Closing.
  Responsible Party: Buyer
  Deadline: Claims must be asserted within survival period (post-closing taxes: 3-year statute from filing date).
  Tax Impact: Buyer's indemnity protects Seller from being stuck with post-closing tax obligations inadvertently allocated to Seller.

TC-010 | Tax Audit Cooperation & Control
  Description: (a) Seller controls audits and contests relating exclusively to pre-closing tax periods, subject to Buyer's right to participate at its own cost if potential liability may flow to Buyer. (b) Buyer controls audits relating to post-closing tax periods. (c) Straddle Period audits are jointly controlled; neither party shall settle without the other's written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld). (d) Each party shall promptly (within 10 business days) notify the other of any Tax Claim relating to the other party's period.
  Responsible Party: Period-specific (see above)
  Deadline: Notice of Tax Claim: within 10 business days of receipt; failure to notify does not forfeit indemnity claim unless actual prejudice results.
  Tax Impact: Cooperation includes providing books, records, and personnel; costs of cooperation borne by requesting party except in Straddle Period audits (shared equally).

TC-011 | FIRPTA Compliance — Day-1 Deliverable
  Description: On the Closing Date, Seller shall deliver to Buyer a valid FIRPTA certification under IRC §1445 certifying that Target (if stock sale) is not a U.S. real property holding corporation (USRPHC), or that Seller is not a foreign person (if asset sale). If certification cannot be made, Buyer shall withhold 15% of the amount realized and remit via Form 8288 within 20 days of Closing.
  Responsible Party: Seller (certification); Buyer (withholding if required)
  Deadline: Day-1 (Closing Date: 2026-10-15); Form 8288 if applicable: 2026-11-04
  Tax Impact: Failure to withhold when required = Buyer liability for 15% of amount realized plus interest and penalties. Buyer may apply for withholding certificate (Form 8288-B) to reduce or eliminate withholding prior to closing.

TC-012 | State & Local Conformity Filings — Day-1 Tax Deliverable
  Description: Within 5 business days post-closing, Tax counsel shall identify all state and local jurisdictions requiring: (i) notice of ownership change; (ii) license or permit transfer/reissuance; (iii) payroll tax account transfer; (iv) sales/use tax account registration update; and (v) independent state §338 election (where applicable). All such filings shall be completed within the applicable statutory deadlines.
  Responsible Party: Buyer's Tax counsel, with Seller's cooperation
  Deadline: T+5 for identification; jurisdiction-specific for filings (range: 10–90 days post-close)
  Tax Impact: Non-compliance triggers successor liability for pre-closing state taxes in bulk-sale states. Unclaimed property filings may also be triggered by change of ownership in certain jurisdictions.

TC-013 | Working Capital True-Up — Tax Treatment
  Description: Any post-closing working capital adjustment (upward or downward) shall be treated as an adjustment to the purchase price for federal and applicable state income tax purposes, allocated consistent with the agreed §1060 / §338 allocation in TC-004. If the adjustment exceeds [$___], the parties shall prepare an amended Form 8594/8883.
  Responsible Party: Tax counsel (joint); Working capital arbitrator determines amount if disputed.
  Deadline: Per APA working capital mechanics (typically T+60 to T+90); amended allocation per STEP-11.
  Tax Impact: Upward WC adjustment increases Buyer's basis in acquired assets (or stock pre-election); downward adjustment reduces basis. Failure to track impacts depreciation/amortization recapture.

TC-014 | Transaction Cost Deductibility — Day-1 Tax Deliverable
  Description: Buyer's tax counsel shall prepare a transaction cost analysis under Rev. Rul. 99-23 and Rev. Proc. 2011-29 within 30 days post-closing to: (i) identify "success-based fees" subject to 70/30 safe harbor election; (ii) separate deductible costs (facilitated vs. non-facilitated) from capitalizable costs; (iii) confirm elections are made on Buyer's timely filed return.
  Responsible Party: Buyer's Tax counsel
  Deadline: Analysis due T+30 (2026-11-14); election on Buyer's return for acquisition year.
  Tax Impact: Proper classification can yield immediate deductions for a meaningful portion of banker, legal, and advisory fees. IRS safe harbor allows 70% deduction of success-based fees without documentation.

TC-015 | R&W Insurance — Tax Matters Coverage Confirmation
  Description: Within 5 business days post-closing, Buyer shall confirm with R&W insurer: (i) binding of the R&W insurance policy; (ii) that tax representations are covered (confirm any tax exclusions or sublimits); (iii) retention/deductible applicable to tax claims; (iv) notice procedures for tax-related claims under the policy.
  Responsible Party: Buyer (insurance procurement); Broker coordinates
  Deadline: T+5 (2026-10-22)
  Tax Impact: R&W insurance is secondary recovery mechanism after Seller indemnity (TC-008). Tax exclusions (e.g., transfer pricing, NOL limitations, §382 issues) must be identified and separately addressed via tax escrow or specific Seller indemnity.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
ESCROW SUMMARY TABLE
─────────────────────────────────────────────

  Escrow Type          | Primary Purpose                        | Trigger for Draw                           | Release Date
  ─────────────────────|────────────────────────────────────────|────────────────────────────────────────────|──────────────
  Tax Escrow (TC-007)  | Pre-closing tax indemnity              | IRS/state assessment; audit settlement     | 2027-10-15*
  Indemnity Escrow     | General R&W indemnity (incl. tax reps) | Indemnification claim per APA              | 2027-10-15*
  WC Escrow            | Working capital true-up settlement     | WC determination finalized (T+60–90)       | ~2026-12-31
  §338 Election Escrow | Seller tax gross-up (if applicable)    | Seller's incremental tax cost confirmed    | T+45 after filing

  * Subject to extension if audit pending (TC-007 terms)

─────────────────────────────────────────────
OPEN ITEMS / FLAGS REQUIRING RESOLUTION
─────────────────────────────────────────────

  FLAG-01: Election decision (§338(h)(10) vs. §336(e) vs. NONE) must be confirmed by STEP-02 deadline (2026-10-08) — currently assumed NONE.
  FLAG-02: State tax clearance certificate status unknown — confirm receipt in all filing jurisdictions before Closing.
  FLAG-03: FIRPTA analysis (USRPHC determination) must be completed by Closing; if Target holds significant real property, withholding may be required.
  FLAG-04: Transfer tax allocation between Buyer and Seller not yet confirmed in APA — resolve before funds flow finalization (STEP-05).
  FLAG-05: R&W insurance binding confirmation timing — confirm binder issued on or before Closing Date.
  FLAG-06: Straddle period identification — confirm whether Target's fiscal year end is 12/31 or other; if other, straddle period mechanics in TC-002 require adjustment.
  FLAG-07: HSR/antitrust clearance — confirm waiting period status; if not yet cleared, Closing Date of 2026-10-15 may need to be extended.
